faq.q: Who exactly was the Constituent Assembly?
faq.a: It was a group of people chosen to write the fundamental laws for India. It gathered together to discuss and write the Constitution.
asks: What was the purpose of the Assembly?

faq.q: What was Dr. Ambedkar's main contribution?
faq.a: He was the chairman of the Drafting Committee, which was responsible for the actual writing of the Constitution. His legal expertise was very important.
asks: Did Ambedkar write the whole thing?
What was his role in the drafting?

faq.q: Was the process easy or difficult?
faq.a: The process was very detailed and involved intense debate among many leaders. They had to consider many different viewpoints.
No, there were many debates about different sections of the law. The assembly had to find compromises that everyone could accept.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Assembly and the Constitution?
faq.a: The Assembly was the group of people doing the writing. The Constitution is the final written document of laws they created.
asks: Is the Constitution the same as the Assembly?

facts: The Constituent Assembly was formed to draft the Constitution of India.
Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
The process involved extensive debate among many leaders.
The Constitution outlines the fundamental laws for the country.

quiz.say: The group tasked with writing the Constitution was called the:
quiz.why: This was the specific body formed for this task.

wrong.0: Parliament is the law-making body, but the Assembly was specifically for drafting the document.
wrong.1: This was only one small committee within the larger Assembly.
wrong.2: This is not the correct historical name for the body.

quiz.say: Who was the chairman of the Drafting Committee?
quiz.why: He was the leading legal mind guiding the drafting process.

wrong.0: He was important for integration, but not the committee chair.
wrong.1: He was a key participant, but not the committee chair.
wrong.3: He was a major leader, but Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

quiz.say: The Constitution establishes the basic rules for:
quiz.why: The Constitution sets out how the country must be run.

wrong.1: The Constitution is broader than just daily parliamentary actions.
wrong.2: It must apply to all citizens, not just one party.
wrong.3: It limits the power of the Prime Minister and government.
